Entry 23
I don't hear much about what the old boss is up to these days—not with these damn ears the way they are. I'll catch a few rumors here and there when our legionnaire remembers to speak up, but they're busy keeping up morale. I said if I ever started slowing them down, I could go back to the scrapyard. Sure, it's boring, but I don't want to be the reason a bunch of cubs end up in early graves.

Entry 35
Got a message from some Blood Legion cub a week ago. Or was it two? Who knows... At my age, time gets a bit fuzzy. This Ranoah Grindsteel has been working on a pet project. Some prototype tank. Cub wrote to every veteran engineer in the damn legions for ordnance input. Says she's offering a chance to see her "baby" up close before some big celebration. Showboaty, but it sounds exciting.
The warband doesn't have me doing much but tinkering these days, so maybe I'll go. I could use a change of scenery and maybe a drink or three.

Entry 41
I think I'm...hearing things. And no, I don't mean my ear's playing tricks on me again. I mean whispers. Thoughts I shouldn't be able to hear. This...voice...keeps asking about the old boss. I think it knows who I was to them. I can't sleep anymore, and Bangar's soldiers watching me like a pack of wolves sure isn't helping.
Ranoah came by to check on me in the morning and had me join her up on the TT6-B. She talked me through the tank specs over and over to keep me present. Reminds me a lot of myself at that age. Glad I jumped at the chance to work on her engineer crew. Gives me something better to do than hobbling around the Black Citadel. Not like the warband will miss me...or even notice that I'm gone...

Entry 50
No whispers since a few days ago. It's all thanks to Imperator Ruinbringer and Centurion Steelcatcher, and no thanks to Jormag. Would it be too much to get a shot off at the ancient wurm before Bangar makes it his pet? Maybe Grindsteel can ask for me.
Speaking of, the crew needs me up top to double-check the deployable gatling guns before we land. We take the beachhead at dusk.

*This once-loved journal is now in tatters. Multiple pages are missing.*  
  
It's been at least a few years since the confessor left us to complete his mission. When I lack inspiration, I look to the note that he left me—my divine ordinance to carve his path while he leads the march against our enemies in Kryta:  
  
"Find a way into Bava Nisos, the city of the Unseen. Saul has guided me here, and our salvation will be revealed. Open the gate."  
  
Until this mission is complete, we will continue to search Janthir. This is my only mission; I've failed too many others in life before. I will do the confessor proud, and Mother will regret calling me visionless and banishing me from my home.  
  
---  
  
There is no sign of any city here—just the ruins of Gavril. I wish I knew more about this destroyed place and the people that lived here before us. Caudceus had found a number of records, but he burned them all right before he left. He said that they contained secrets from Saul that were meant for his eyes only, and that we were not worthy. Judge has expressed some skepticism of this, especially as years have passed, but Tatyanna is devout. She prays every single day.  
  
We've managed to carve out a nice-enough home here in the remains of Gavril—while most of the ruins are inaccessible, Judge was able to clear a path into the old village inn. Most of the building interior is blocked by rubble, but there's enough space. Tatyanna has her own room, and Judge and I sleep in the "kitchen" (the kitchen being one pot for boiling and a basket of food). It's a productive home.  
  
---  
  
While Judge and I were avoiding a small kodan party that has ventured to the isle, a blast of energy knocked us from our feet. My ears rang and my nose started to bleed—just like the last time we tried to cross farther into the bay. We rushed back to Tatyanna.  
  
We searched the isle, avoiding the kodan, but it was unchanged. Right before we turned back toward the inn, Judge's attention snapped to the northern bay. Off in the distance, probably a day's row away, a rock formation peeked out from the fog. I never noticed it before.  
  
My mind swam, searching through images from our prior voyages—days spent fishing at this exact spot. It was as if that rock had been there all along, but it had a freshness that gave me a headache. Judge rubbed his temple—his head hurt too. Tatyanna recalled how certain mesmer enchantments can give you a similar headache, especially those that manipulate our thoughts. Perhaps, she said, we were just under a spell.

*The following report collects the content of Project Omega subject Zipp's audio logs, as transcribed by project specialist Keelli, for Overseer Kuda's eyes only. Unauthorized access will be reported and prosecuted according to Inquest compliance protocols.*  
  
**Entry 5**  
DIE! DIE! Commander must die! It wasn't Zipp's fault, Overseer Kuda. Zipp was just excited! Zipp will do better. I will do better. Sorry. I... I... Stop. I am Zipp. I am Zipp. Zipp is me. We lost. We lost... It was terrible. Next time, the commander will die. And the others. They'll all suffer. Overseer will see it done.  
  
**Entry 6**  
Running helped. For a while. Not as easy... It's getting harder. Mind still races. Zipp is too fast. I'm too fast. I'm not... I can't... Overseer, help. Please. I... It's too much. Too much. Can't stop. Thinking. Speeding. Fast. Fast. Should my head...should it hurt this bad? Eyes burn.   
  
**Entry 7**  
They're coming! Commander is coming! Zipp will have another chance! Learned fast. We learned. We don't play. We have to win! It won't end. Not like this. Not like last time! Plokk. Naati. Zipp. Zipp. Zipp! I am Zipp! It will be their end. Come to us, Commander. Come.

It's amazing that despite their own creation turning against them, the people of Kaineng are still surviving! Of course, it's likely the only way they're surviving is through the shared knowledge of the Speakers and the Kestrels who, even in this reality, continue to fight back. I think that says a lot about their morals; so strong, they transcend from reality to reality. And, well, they're gonna need it fighting against the Kryptis.  

It's impressive that they're able to run patrols inside of the city to gain information on the construct's movements, but it's upsetting that the only way these two groups worked together is by uniting against a common foe... I should be used to it. The same happened with the Elder Dragons, after all.  

Now that the Elder Dragon of the ocean is gone, maybe the world can catch a break. I'd love to see Rata Sum undergo some big changes. That place needs one heck of a system reboot.

It is a mistake that many make to say that hunters are damaging nature. After all, are we not part of nature? When we tracked a deer by endurance alone, claiming it only when exhaustion overtook it, with nothing but our bare hands, were we not part of nature then? Why then would a bow of wood and animal sinew make us unnatural?  
  
The hunt is not about the desecration of nature but the celebration of our history and our traditions. So long as we do not overhunt or act cruelly in taking our prey, we are not doing a dishonorable thing. We are a part of the same cycle as our prey, and it's best we never forget that.
